meta.heading: Round 1: before any code
meta.intro: Five decisions I need before scaffolding milestone M0. My pick is already selected on each card; press Approve, or write a note and press Needs changes. Everything saves as you go, and new cards appear here without reloading the page.

r1-name.title: Call the app Shiftbook everywhere
body: The docs say **Work Tracker** and leave the backup extension to "the final app name". The repo is called **Shiftbook**. The name ends up in the window title, the data folder, the installer and the backup files, so it is cheapest to settle now.
The app identifier also sets the folder your data lives in (for example `%APPDATA%\<identifier>` on Windows). Changing it later means moving data, so it is part of this card.

options.why: Matches the repo. I would update the docs to say Shiftbook in the same commit as the scaffold.
Keep the docs as written; the repo name stays Shiftbook.
Clearly belongs to Shiftbook; nothing else uses it.
Ties it to this GitHub repo. Safe while it is a personal tool.
Pick this if IT wants it treated as a company app.

r1-name.pick: Shiftbook, `.shiftbak`, and the GitHub-based identifier unless IT says it should be a company app.

r1-scratch.title: What "start from scratch" means for this repo
body: Here is how I read it. The repo was empty. I committed your docs unchanged as the first commit ("Add spec and project docs"). No code from Fathom is reused; only the idea of this sign-off sheet carries over.
From here I go one milestone at a time, starting with M0. I stop at the end of each one and bring the next questions here.

options.why: Start M0 once the cards in this round are approved.
Before any code, I read the spec closely and bring every gap or contradiction I find here as a card.

questions.legend: Anything in the docs you already know is out of date? (optional)

r1-scratch.pick: Yes. I will raise doc gaps as cards when a milestone runs into them, instead of reviewing everything up front.

r1-deps.title: Dependencies for the M0 scaffold
body: CLAUDE.md asks me to list every dependency and wait for your OK. M0 only needs enough to open a blank Today page and run CI. The database, encryption and file dialogs come in M1 and later, and I will ask again then.
Each package goes in at its newest stable version, pinned by `Cargo.lock` and `package-lock.json`.

head: Package
Where
Why
On the pre-approved list
rows: Passing data between the Rust core and the UI
Lets Vite build Svelte files. Svelte cannot be used with Vite without it.
Type-checks `.svelte` files. This is what `npm run check` runs.
Runs `npm run tauri dev` and builds installers

head: CI action
Why
rows: GitHub's own: get the code, install Node
Installs Rust with fmt and clippy
Caches Rust builds so CI takes minutes, not half an hour
Installed in CI only: checks crates for known vulnerabilities

bullets: No router package: there are only eight screens, so a small store handles switching between them.
No CSS framework, icon font or web font. Everything ships inside the app (no network).

options.why: The four packages not on the list are the standard companions to the approved ones.

options.value: Approve, but use the Rust CLI
options.why: Swap `@tauri-apps/cli` for `cargo install tauri-cli`. One fewer npm package; slower first setup.
Tell me which ones in the note.

r1-shell.title: Where the menu goes: side or top
body: M0 only needs a blank Today page, but the menu frame gets built now. Both mockups below show the Today screen from SPEC §2.1 with sample data. Nothing is styled for real yet; this is about layout only.

figures.caption: **A · Menu on the left.** Always visible, room for all eight screens and a Lock button at the bottom.
**B · Menu across the top.** More width for the Time Log table; gets crowded on a small laptop screen.

options.why: Easiest to scan and click. Can collapse to icons later if you want the width back.
As the spec says. Light when Windows is light, dark when it is dark.

options.value: Follow Windows, with a manual switch in Settings

r1-shell.pick: A, following the Windows theme. I'll bring real visual design (colours, type) as its own card in M2, once there is a working screen to dress.

r1-it.title: Has IT OK'd a self-built app for work notes?
body: START_HERE and SECURITY.md both say to check with IT before real work data goes in, and whether the code should live in a company GitHub organisation. This doesn't block building. It decides when your real data goes in, and possibly the app identifier on the naming card.

options.why: Tell me in the note if they said anything about where the repo should live.
I build and test with sample data only.
Same as above. I'll ask again before M6 (importing your Excel data).

r1-it.pick: Your answer here. I don't need the real data until M6, so nothing waits on this.

r1-sheet.title: How we work on this sheet
body: This page is where I bring questions, mockups and screenshots, and where you decide. It keeps working while you are on it. New cards and updates arrive live without reloading the page. If I change a card while you are typing in it, the card stays put and a **Show the new version** button appears instead.

When a round is done I move its cards to **Archive**, where they stay searchable for both of us. Your decisions and notes are stored with the page, so I can read them in any later session, not only this one. **Notes to Claude** is for anything that doesn't fit a card; I answer underneath each note.
bullets: Mockups are live HTML, so some can be clicked through. Screenshots of the real app come in from M0 onward.
Every decision you approve also goes into `docs/DECISIONS.md` in the repo, so the code history records why.
Your typing saves after a short pause. If you are offline, it stays in your browser and goes up when you're back.

questions.legend: Anything else you want from it?

options.value: A short milestone summary card at the end of each milestone
options.why: What was built, what to try, and a screenshot.

options.value: A Decisions tab: one table of everything approved so far
options.why: Handy once there are a few rounds. It's in the repo either way.

r1-sheet.pick: Approve as is. Tell me in the note if anything about the sheet gets in your way, and I'll fix the sheet first.
